fact: Subsea Cables & Internet Infrastructure reports the 2Africa cable's Ivory Coast branch back in service, repair declared complete and all services live on Friday morning Abidjan time after being up and down since Wednesday (outage repaired, not a closure).
Equinix states that MainOne's submarine network from Portugal to Lagos, Accra and the West African coast has landing stations in Nigeria, Ghana and Cote d'Ivoire.
MainOne announced its cable branch to Cote d'Ivoire in service and ready for first customers, landed at Grand Bassam beach, Abidjan, with a cable landing station there.

Mobile Europe reports CSquared, a wholesale operator, added capacity on the 2Africa West system, described as an open-access system; the article places Abidjan among 2Africa/West African landing-station cities.

fact: Equinix states that it took full ownership and operational control of the MainOne submarine cable system (about 7,000 km, Portugal to Nigeria) on closing 5 April 2022, with landing stations in Nigeria, Ghana, Cote d'Ivoire (Abidjan) and Portugal.

The record on Maroc Telecom's 9,414 km West Africa submarine cable states it has a landing point at Abidjan, Cote d'Ivoire, and that the south segment (Casablanca to CIV, Togo, Benin, Gabon, Mauritania; 20 Tbps) became operational in July 2021.

fact: Developing Telecoms says Cote d'Ivoire hosts landing points for six subsea cables: 2Africa, ACE, MainOne, Maroc Telecom West Africa, SAT-3/WASC and WACS.
MainOne says it landed its submarine cable in Cote d'Ivoire before launching its first data centre there in 2019, and delivers connectivity over it.
